info.name: Base64 Convertor API
info.description: Complete API collection for the Base64 Convertor Spring Boot service. Import and set the {{baseUrl}} variable to your host (default: http://localhost:8080).

request.description:
Downloads the file at `url` (via HTTP POST with optional cookie/payload) and returns Base64.

Also writes the Base64 to a `.b64` file on disk (path logged at INFO level).

**Required:** `url`
**Optional:** `cookie` (JSESSIONID value), `payload` (raw string body to POST to the URL)

**Retry:** Up to `app.retry.max-attempts` times with exponential backoff on failure.

Advanced endpoint with full control over the outbound HTTP request.

**Required:** `url`
**Optional:**
- `httpMethod` — `GET` or `POST` (default `POST`)
- `cookie` — full Cookie header value
- `authorization` — Authorization header value (Bearer token, Basic, etc.)
- `payload` — JSON object; if it contains a `headers` key, those are merged into the outbound request headers; the rest of the payload is sent as the POST body

**Auto-detects:**
- MIME type from `Content-Type` response header (falls back to magic bytes)
- File name from `Content-Disposition` header (falls back to URL path)

**Validates:**
- Magic bytes match declared MIME type
- Response is not an HTML/JSON error page
- File size ≤ `app.pdf.stream-threshold-bytes`

**Also writes .b64 file to disk.**

item.name: Convert to Base64 (Dynamic – POST with auth)

request.description:
Same dynamic endpoint but demonstrating authenticated POST with custom headers and a body payload.

The `payload.headers` map is extracted and added as HTTP headers on the outbound request. All other payload keys are sent as the JSON POST body.

Downloads each file, converts to Base64, injects `attachmentData` into the message envelope, then POSTs the full message to `target_url`.

**Flow:**
1. Fetch file from `url` (with optional `cookie`/`payload`)
2. Set `message.content.attachment.attachmentData = <base64>`
3. POST envelope to `target_url` with `target_auth` header (falls back to `app.default.auth.token`)
4. Returns result per file

**`attachmentData` is cleared from the response** after forwarding (not echoed back).

Same as PDF Send (Batch) but accepts a single request object instead of an array.

If `target_url` is blank or null, the file is converted but NOT forwarded — only the Base64 response is returned.

Decodes `base64DocContent`, validates it is a genuine PDF (magic-byte check), optionally applies AES-256 password protection via Apache PDFBox, and returns the result inside the standard ApiResponse envelope.

**Required:** `passwordProtected`, `base64DocContent`
**Conditionally required:** `password` — mandatory only when `passwordProtected=true`
**Optional:** `responseType` — `BASE64` (default, also what you get if this field is omitted entirely, for backward compatibility) or `ATTACHMENT`

**Max size:** `pdf.protection.max-file-size-mb` (default 20MB decoded)

Every response (success or failure) carries `X-Request-Id`, `X-API-Version`, `X-Timestamp` headers, and `data.base64ProtectedPdf`'s `requestId` field in the body always matches the `X-Request-Id` header.

Same endpoint, same request shape, only `responseType` differs — returns the protected PDF as a raw binary download (`application/pdf`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`) instead of a JSON envelope. Controller branches on `responseType`; the service layer itself stays transport-agnostic (always returns `byte[]`).

`password` is conditionally required — mandatory only when `passwordProtected=true`. This cross-field rule is enforced in the service layer (not bean validation), so it returns the ApiResponse error envelope, not Spring's default validation-failure shape.

response.name: 400 Bad Request
response.body:
{
  "status": "FAILED",
  "message": "Password is mandatory when password protection is enabled",
  "data": null,
  "timestamp": "2026-07-02T18:10:00.123Z",
  "requestId": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890"
}

request.description: `responseType` only accepts `BASE64` or `ATTACHMENT`. An unrecognized value fails Jackson enum deserialization before the controller method even runs, and Spring's default handling for an unreadable request body returns 400 (verified live — this codebase has no global @ControllerAdvice, so this relies on Spring MVC's own default behavior, not custom code).
Only reproducible when `pdf.protection.enabled=false` (default `true`) — included for completeness of the documented failure surface, not runnable against a default-config instance.

Decodes `base64DocContent`, validates it is a genuine PDF (magic-byte check), best-effort extracts statement fields (`statementDate`, `totalAmountDue`, `minimumAmountDue`, `paymentDueDate`) from the document's text content, optionally applies AES-256 password protection via Apache PDFBox, and returns everything inside the standard ApiResponse envelope.

Same request contract as `/pdf/protect` (see PDF Protection folder) — this is a sibling endpoint, not a divergent one.

**Required:** `passwordProtected`, `base64DocContent`
**Conditionally required:** `password` — mandatory only when `passwordProtected=true`
**Optional:** `responseType` — `BASE64` (default) or `ATTACHMENT`

**Statement field extraction is best-effort:** a field whose configured label (`pdf.bandhan.field-labels.*`) isn't found in the document text is returned as `null` — it never fails the request, since password protection is the primary responsibility. Labels are configurable via `application.properties`, so adding a new field (e.g. Customer Name) requires no code change.

**Max size:** `pdf.protection.max-file-size-mb` (default 20MB decoded, shared with `/pdf/protect`).

response.name: 200 OK - JSON with Base64 and extracted fields

item.name: Protect Bandhan Statement - ATTACHMENT response (binary download)

request.description:
Same endpoint, same request shape, only `responseType` differs — returns the protected PDF as a raw binary download (`application/pdf`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`) instead of a JSON envelope.

**Note:** the extracted statement fields (`statementDate`, `totalAmountDue`, `minimumAmountDue`, `paymentDueDate`) are only carried in the JSON/BASE64 response shape — there is no channel to include them in a raw binary body, so ATTACHMENT mode returns just the protected PDF bytes, same as `/pdf/protect`.

item.name: Protect Bandhan Statement - fields not found (best-effort null)

request.description: Demonstrates the best-effort contract: this is a genuine, valid PDF (passes the magic-byte check) but its page has no text content stream, so none of the four configured labels (`Statement Date`, `Total Amount Due`, `Minimum Amount Due`, `Payment Due Date`) can be found. The request still succeeds — the PDF is returned/protected normally — and every extracted field is individually `null` rather than the whole call failing.

response.name: 200 OK - all fields null
response.body:
{
  "status": "SUCCESS",
  "message": "PDF generated successfully",

request.description:
Spring Boot Actuator health endpoint. Returns component-level health.

Runs on port 9090 (set by `management.server.port`).

Prometheus scrape endpoint. Returns all metrics in text exposition format.

Key custom metrics:
- `base64_conversions_total{status="success"|"failure"}`
- `base64_conversion_duration_seconds`
- `pdf_conversions_total{status="success"|"failure"}`
- `pdf_conversion_duration_seconds`
- `base64_output_files_written_total`
- `base64_output_files_deleted_total`
- `base64_output_files_errors_total`
Lists all available metric names in JSON. Use the individual metric name endpoint to drill down.
Shows the total count of PDF conversions, tagged by `status=success` or `status=failure`.
Total number of `.b64` output files written to disk since the service started.
Returns application info (name, version, description from pom.xml if configured).
